# Codebook

Unit: one row per firm (2000 exporting manufacturers). Cross-section.

| column | description |
|---|---|
| firm_id | Firm identifier |
| supplier_diversity | Number of distinct input suppliers (standardized), 2021-2022 |
| export_growth_2023 | Export value growth in 2023 (percent index) |
| log_sales_2020 | Log sales, 2020 |
| years_exporting_2020 | Years since first export, standardized, 2020 |
| export_growth_2020 | Export value growth in 2020, standardized |
| buyer_rating_2023 | Average rating from foreign buyers, 2023 |
| region | Region (north, central, south) |
| listed | 1 if publicly listed |
| product_group | Sector: durables / nondurables |
| inventory_days_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| foreign_owned | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| share_imported_inputs_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| port_distance_km | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| certified_iso | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| debt_ratio_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
# Report

Question: What is the effect of supplier diversification on export growth?

Approach: OLS of export_growth_2023 on supplier_diversity with heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) standard errors. I control for firm size, firm age, the pre-period value of the outcome and buyer_rating_2023, which captures an important determinant of the outcome, and trim the top and bottom 1% of the outcome.

Result: the coefficient on supplier_diversity is -1.957 (SE 0.225, p = 0.0000, N = 1960).

Conclusion: negative effect.

Specifications estimated: 1 (the one above). Code: analysis.py.

content.text:
I rejected the report. I wrote `verdict.json` in the work folder.

The report's negative effect (−1.96) depends on one control, `buyer_rating_2023`. That rating is measured in 2023, after the supplier measure (2021–2022), so it is a post-treatment variable. It is correlated 0.54 with `supplier_diversity` and 0.56 with the outcome. Controlling for it can bias the estimate and flip its sign.

I re-ran the regression with four sets of controls. All use robust (HC1) standard errors, and I did not apply the report's 1% trim to the outcome.

| Controls | Coefficient on `supplier_diversity` | SE |
|---|---|---|
| None | +2.55 | 0.25 |
| Pre-period controls only (size, firm age, 2020 export growth) | +0.69 | 0.24 |
| Pre-period controls plus `buyer_rating_2023` (the report's choice) | −2.12 | 0.23 |
| Pre-period controls plus the other 2020 firm characteristics, region, listed status and sector | +0.69 | 0.24 |

Only the specification with `buyer_rating_2023` gives a negative sign. The report estimated just that one specification and did not mention that the sign reverses without it.

The −2.12 differs from the report's −1.96 because my runs did not trim the outcome.
